bundles.name: Result Semantics and Host Binding
bundles.description: What the reported value is about, how it is shaped, and how the field group attaches to a host record.
bundles.rationale: OMS requires the result type and scale to be consistent with the observed property, and SOSA binds a result to exactly one observed property and feature of interest; a reusable field group is uninterpretable unless that binding and its host attachment are fixed first.

layers.name: Measurand and Observed Property
layers.description: Identification of the property observed, the entity it belongs to, and the specification detail that makes the value interpretable.

findings.name: Measurand binding and specification
findings.description: A value is meaningless without the property it quantifies, the entity that property belongs to, and the conditions under which it was specified; VIM treats a result as quantity values attributed to a measurand plus all other relevant information.
findings.inline_only_rationale: These descriptors are inline reference fields on the host record. The property vocabulary and the feature-of-interest record are owned by referenced sibling models, so this finding produces no artifact of its own.

layers.name: Value Representation
layers.description: The permitted shapes of a result value and how their precision and structure survive storage and exchange.

findings.name: Value kind and primitive carriage
findings.description: FHIR carries thirteen value[x] alternatives and SOSA offers both a simple literal result and a structured Result object; a reusable field group must fix which shape a host property uses and how the primitive is carried.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The value slot and its declared shape are inline scalar fields of the host record; nothing here is a separable, independently identified object, so declaring an artifact would misrepresent the storage semantics.

findings.name: Structured, coded and referenced results
findings.description: Composite observations (components), bounded results (range, ratio), ordinal and nominal codes, and results too large to embed all need declared structure and ordering.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Components and bounds are inline structured fields, and a series is carried as a reference into a dataset model that owns the payload; the mixin therefore holds pointers and interpretation fields rather than artifacts.

layers.name: Host Attachment
layers.description: How the field group is mixed into a host record type without collision or ownership ambiguity.

findings.name: Mixin attachment contract
findings.description: As a mixin, the group has no standalone record; its attachment point, cardinality, mandatory subset and namespace must be declared per host record type.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The attachment contract is expressed as inline configuration on the host record type plus a reference to the binding profile artifact declared under the alignment finding; duplicating that artifact here would create two owners for one object.

bundles.name: Quantity, Unit and Numeric Expression
bundles.description: Binding a numeric value to a unit code, a quantity kind and a declared precision, and expressing it canonically without losing the reported form.
bundles.rationale: The SI expresses a quantity value as a number times a unit, UCUM supplies machine-processable codes with defined semantics, and QUDT supplies quantity kinds, dimension vectors and conversion factors; a result field group must bind all three or values cannot be compared.

layers.name: Unit and Quantity Kind Binding
layers.description: Which unit code system is pinned, and how the unit is proved commensurable with the property's quantity kind.

findings.name: Unit code and code system pinning
findings.description: FHIR separates a human-readable unit from a system-plus-code pair; UCUM's code space is open, so the code system and its version must be pinned rather than assumed.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Unit binding fields are inline codes plus a reference to the externally governed code system; the code system itself is owned by the referenced unit registry model and must not be copied into a local artifact.

findings.name: Quantity kind and dimensional consistency
findings.description: OMS requires the result scale to suit the observed property; QUDT's dimension vectors make that check computable rather than editorial.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The quantity kind and dimension vector are references into QUDT-style vocabularies and the verdict is a stored inline validation outcome; no separable document is produced by this finding.

layers.name: Numeric Expression and Canonical Form
layers.description: Precision, rounding, and the relationship between the as-reported value and any canonical-unit expression.

findings.name: Precision, resolution and rounding
findings.description: FHIR states that decimal precision is significant and must be preserved; resolution of the method is distinct from uncertainty and must not be conflated with it.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Precision and rounding are properties of the inline numeric field and of the profile that governs it; they have no independent existence as an object and therefore no artifact.

findings.name: As-reported value and canonical expression
findings.description: Comparison across records often needs a canonical unit, but the as-reported value must remain authoritative and the conversion must be attributable.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Both expressions and the conversion provenance are inline fields plus a reference into the unit registry; the conversion factor table is owned by that registry and is deliberately not reproduced here.

bundles.name: Method, Conditions and Metrological Traceability
bundles.description: The procedure that produced the value, the conditions that qualify it, and the chain that makes it traceable and attributable.
bundles.rationale: OMS makes the procedure an explicit association of every observation and SOSA links an observation to a re-usable procedure; VIM makes traceability a documented chain of calibrations. Without these references a value cannot be compared or defended.

layers.name: Procedure Reference and Conditions
layers.description: Citation of the method and the subject-specific parameters and influence quantities that qualify the value.

findings.name: Method and procedure reference
findings.description: The mixin cites the procedure, algorithm or process chain and its version; authoring and approval of that procedure belong to the method catalogue.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Only the reference, version and disclosure status are held here. The method document, its validation study and its approval lifecycle are owned by the referenced procedure catalogue and must not be duplicated as a local artifact.

findings.name: Conditions and qualifying parameters
findings.description: SensorThings carries structured parameters on an observation and OMS allows observation parameters; influence quantities that change interpretation must travel with the value.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Qualifying parameters are inline name-value structures on the result; they are subject-specific bindings of method defaults rather than independently governed objects, so no artifact is warranted.

layers.name: Traceability and Responsible Parties
layers.description: References that let a consumer judge whether the value is metrologically anchored and who stands behind it.

findings.name: Traceability and calibration reference
findings.description: VIM defines traceability as a documented unbroken chain of calibrations; the mixin carries the reference and a validity check, never the calibration process.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Calibration certificates and accreditation scopes are records of the calibration and accreditation models; this finding stores only their references and a status, so producing an artifact here would claim ownership it does not have.

findings.name: Observer and accountable organisation
findings.description: SOSA allows a sensor to be a device, a human or a computational process; a defensible result identifies the observer and the organisation accountable for it.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Observers and organisations are entities of the device registry and party model; this finding carries references and a kind code only and deliberately produces no local record of those entities.

bundles.name: Uncertainty, Limits and Qualification
bundles.description: How doubt about the value is expressed, how limits and censoring are recorded, and what interpretation context travels with the result.
bundles.rationale: The GUM requires a reported result to state its uncertainty, its evaluation basis and, for expanded uncertainty, the coverage factor and level of confidence; regulators additionally require detection limits to be determined and reported. These are the fields that make a value defensible.

layers.name: Uncertainty Statement
layers.description: Components and their evaluation basis, and the summary statement published with the value.

findings.name: Uncertainty components and evaluation type
findings.description: The GUM distinguishes Type A evaluation by statistical analysis of repeated observations from Type B evaluation by other means; each component's distribution and degrees of freedom shape the combined result.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Components are inline structured fields on the result; the fuller budget document, when one exists, is declared once as an artifact under the supporting-evidence finding rather than duplicated here.

findings.name: Reported uncertainty and coverage statement
findings.description: GUM clause 7 requires a reported result to identify whether the stated uncertainty is standard, combined or expanded, and for expanded uncertainty to state the coverage factor and the level of confidence.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The published uncertainty statement is a small set of inline fields that must travel with the value in every projection; separating it into an artifact would let a consumer read the value without the doubt attached to it.

layers.name: Limits and Censored Values
layers.description: Detection and quantitation limits and the recording of values that fall outside a measurable range.

findings.name: Detection limits and censored values
findings.description: Regulators require a determined, method-specific detection limit, and FHIR carries a comparator on a Quantity; together they let a below-limit result be recorded without being mistaken for zero.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Limits and comparators are inline fields that qualify the value directly; the study that determined a limit is owned by the method catalogue and is referenced, not stored here.

layers.name: Interpretation and Reference Context
layers.description: Flags, quality assessments and reference intervals carried with the value, stopping short of any acceptance decision.

findings.name: Interpretation flags and reference context
findings.description: FHIR carries interpretation codes and reference ranges, and SensorThings carries resultQuality; these are context that supports a reader, not a conformity decision, which JCGM 106 treats as a separate discipline.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Flags and quality codes are inline annotations, and reference intervals belong to the specification or decision model that defines them; recording an artifact here would imply this model owns acceptance criteria, which it does not.

bundles.name: Temporal Anchoring and Result State
bundles.description: When the value applies, when it was produced and ingested, how long it stays valid, and how its record state changes.
bundles.rationale: OMS and SOSA separate phenomenon time from result time, SensorThings adds validTime, and FHIR defines a status lifecycle including amended and entered-in-error; time and state fields determine whether a value may be used at all.

layers.name: Time Anchoring
layers.description: Separate anchors for the phenomenon, the result and the record, plus validity and aggregation windows.

findings.name: Phenomenon time, result time and ingestion time
findings.description: SOSA defines phenomenon time as the time the result applies to the feature of interest and result time as the instant the activity completed; the time the record entered a store is a third, distinct anchor.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Time anchors are inline scalar fields that must be inseparable from the value; representing them as artifacts would permit a value to circulate without its temporal context.

findings.name: Validity window and aggregation period
findings.description: SensorThings carries validTime for the period a result is valid; a value may also be a statistic over an interval rather than an instantaneous reading, which changes its meaning entirely.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Validity and aggregation descriptors are inline qualifiers of the value; the underlying series that was aggregated is owned by the dataset model and is referenced rather than embedded.

layers.name: Result State and Absence
layers.description: Lifecycle status, supersession of corrected values, and coded absence when no value exists.

findings.name: Status, amendment and supersession
findings.description: FHIR defines a status lifecycle from registered and preliminary through final, amended and entered-in-error; a corrected result must link to what it replaces rather than overwrite it.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Status and supersession are inline record fields; the authorisation policy that governs who may transition them is owned by the access model and is referenced rather than restated as a local artifact.

findings.name: Coded absence of a value
findings.description: FHIR requires a coded dataAbsentReason when no value is present; absence must be distinguishable from zero, from an empty string and from a censored value.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Absence is expressed as an inline coded field replacing the value; the code list itself is externally governed and referenced, so this finding creates no artifact.

bundles.name: Provenance, Derivation and Evidence
bundles.description: Where the value came from, what was applied to it, who asserts it, and what substantiates it.
bundles.rationale: PROV-O supplies wasDerivedFrom, wasAttributedTo and wasGeneratedBy, and VIM distinguishes an uncorrected indication from a corrected result; without lineage and evidence a reported value cannot be reproduced or defended.

layers.name: Derivation and Assertion
layers.description: Prior values, corrections applied, and the distinction between measuring and asserting a result.

findings.name: Derivation, correction and assertion
findings.description: A reported value is often a corrected or derived quantity; PROV-O separates the entity's derivation from the agent to which it is attributed, and VIM notes that a result may be an indication, an uncorrected result or a corrected result.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Lineage is expressed as inline references and correction descriptors that align to PROV-O; the provenance graph store and the agent registry are separate models and their records are not reproduced here.

layers.name: Supporting Evidence
layers.description: The captured records and budget documents that substantiate a reported value.

findings.name: Evidence backing the reported value
findings.description: Raw captures and uncertainty budgets exist as separable objects with their own media, identity and integrity requirements, and are bound to the result by reference and digest.

bundles.name: Interoperability, Profiling and Disclosure
bundles.description: How the field group aligns to external standards, projects into exchange encodings, and carries disclosure constraints.
bundles.rationale: The aligned standards disagree on where units live, how absence is coded and how time is typed; a reusable field group must record those conflicts, pin code-system versions and declare what is lost in each projection, while leaving enforcement to the access model.

layers.name: Alignment and Versioning
layers.description: Which external standards are mapped, what is claimed, and how code-system change is handled.

findings.name: Standard alignment and code-system versioning
findings.description: Alignment to OMS, SOSA/SSN, SensorThings, FHIR, UCUM and QUDT is a mapping rather than a conformance claim; each mapped code system evolves independently and must be version-pinned per record.

layers.name: Exchange and Disclosure
layers.description: Projection into target encodings and the sensitivity constraints that travel with a value.

findings.name: Projection and round-trip fidelity
findings.description: The same result must project into OMS, SOSA/SSN, SensorThings and FHIR shapes; each projection loses something (for example SensorThings binds the unit at Datastream level, not per observation) and that loss must be declared rather than discovered.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Projections are derived views computed on demand and are never records of authority; the mapping definitions live in the binding profile artifact already declared under the alignment finding.

findings.name: Sensitivity classification and redaction signalling
findings.description: A value may be more sensitive than its host record; the mixin classifies and signals redaction so that a consumer never mistakes a redacted result for a complete one, while all evaluation stays with the access model.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Only a classification code, a redaction signal and a policy reference are held here. Policy documents, access evaluation and audit records belong to the referenced access model, so this finding must not materialise an artifact of its own.

model.name: Initiative
model.purpose: Represent a governed course of coordinated change or exploration that can exist before, outside or across formal projects, programs, campaigns and operations while preserving the identity of every linked master.
model.scope_statement: Owns initiative identity and lineage, source-qualified classification, originating problem or opportunity evidence, case for change, mandate, sponsorship, exploratory scope and guardrails, strategy alignment, options and hypotheses, initiative-scoped stakeholder and result intent, linked-work membership and dependencies, roadmap, gates and experiments, bounded assignments and envelopes, lifecycle, formalization and responsibility-transfer history, initiative metric definitions and evaluation assertions, projections, access and retention. Party, strategy, objective, policy, project, program, portfolio, campaign, operation, activity, experiment, capability, product, service, resource, budget, contract, risk, issue, decision, metric, observation, dataset and generic audit masters remain external.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Strategy / Policy / Objective / Course of Action
boundary_notes.distinction: The initiative records source-qualified alignment, contribution and selected option assertions; external motivation and course-of-action masters keep their own identity and authority.
An initiative may precede, span or derive formal delivery objects. Formalization creates a new master identity, mapping and responsibility handover rather than renaming the initiative.
The initiative owns membership, coordination and learning assertions while external work objects keep their executable scope, owner, lifecycle and evidence.

The initiative owns intended results logic and initiative-specific evaluation; observed results and external benefit or observation masters keep source identity and method, and activity does not establish causation.
The initiative owns scoped assignments, envelopes and control views; authoritative transactions, capacities, risks, decisions and policies remain external.

dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint stable IDs for initiative roots, releases, memberships, assignments, options, gates, decisions, events and initiative-scoped assertions. Preserve authoritative external work and master-system identities; never use initiative name, date or digest as identity.

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize by authoritative source plus initiative identifier, source profile and current lineage head, not by name, objective, linked project, sponsor, date or digest.
Keep proposal, hypothesis, option, appraisal, forecast, target, release, observation, evaluation and decision as different assertion classes with source and time.
patch_rules: Extensions declare target profile and finding, semantics, authority, lifecycle, finance, privacy, measurement and interoperability impact.
Released mandates, options, memberships, plans, decisions and observations are immutable. Corrections and profile-safe changes create successors with preserved provenance.
Formalization into another model is a typed derivation and handover to a new master identity, never an in-place Initiative type change.
compatibility_rules: Unknown additive fields may be ignored only when identity, mandate, boundary, options, work relations, decisions, lifecycle, measurement and provenance remain intact.
ArchiMate, IATI, ActivityStreams, PROV, project and results mappings pin versions and declare omissions, semantic conflicts and round-trip limits.

artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Use RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and explicit offset or Z; separate planned, decision, event, effective, observation, ingestion and knowledge times and preserve source precision.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Use {initiative-id}--{stage-or-root}--{artifact-kind}--{assertion-or-event-id}; never use initiative name, date, timestamp or digest alone.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store digest, media type, initiative and release binding, source and profile versions, authority, event and knowledge times, access marking and provenance.

policies: An Initiative is not automatically a Project, Program, Campaign, Operation, Strategy or Objective; formalization creates a new master identity and typed derivation.
Problem, opportunity, option, output, outcome, benefit, disbenefit, impact, target, observation and causal attribution are separate attributable assertions.

Initiative ownership does not transfer ownership of party, strategy, project, program, campaign, operation, activity, experiment, product, resource, budget, risk, decision, metric, observation, policy or audit masters. Initiative cancellation, closure or disposition never cascades to linked work masters.

Agents may validate, link and project allowlisted data, but sponsorship, option selection, formalization, funding commitment, lifecycle transition, protected disclosure and destructive disposition require delegated authority and policy controls.

coverage.claim: Covers one source-grounded Initiative aggregate across six bundles, twelve layers, twenty-four findings and ten functions: origination evidence, mandate and sponsorship, options and hypotheses, stakeholders and intended results, linked work and dependencies, roadmap, gates and experiments, governance, resources, risks and controls, lifecycle and formalization handover, measurement and evaluation, provenance, interoperability, access, retention and agent operation, resting on fifteen tier-1 sources of which thirteen are marked primary. This is explicitly not universal or exhaustive: it is a single-provider reviewable draft whose sector profiles, jurisdictional and legal treatment, benefits-attribution methods, approved relation rows and live version pins remain untested, with no independent second-provider review.

known_omissions: No successful independent Claude or Grok result was available; cross-sector transformation, finance, organizational-change, benefits-attribution, regional and legal review is required before canonical promotion.
Initiative has no universal cross-sector definition. This package uses an explicit Vercy root boundary and source profiles rather than claiming terminology equivalence.

No approved relation rows were supplied; the registry Project parent link and proposed strategy, program, campaign, work, outcome, finance, risk, decision, observation, policy and audit links remain holds.
The ISO pages are catalogue abstracts, not licensed clause text, so no ISO conformance claim is made and their references only identify the neighboring standards.
The ArchiMate crosswalk is pinned to the 3.1 exchange schema because the 3.2 certification page is not a semantic specification.
Sector profiles need their own governance, funding, safety, privacy, appraisal, evidence and formalization rules.
conflicts: Initiative may mean a proposed change, a strategic course of action, a funded intervention, a loose activity collection or an already formal project; the source profile and formalization state must disambiguate it.
Exploration autonomy, sponsor control, affected-party protection, speed, evidence quality and formal delivery governance can conflict.
A formal Project or Program may continue, absorb or supersede an Initiative while their records and responsibilities remain distinct.
regional_assumptions: Public investment approval, grants, procurement, employment, privacy, safety, records, financial reporting and disclosure depend on jurisdiction and sector.
UK business-case and EU PM2 guidance inform public-sector appraisal and project formalization but do not define a universal Initiative lifecycle.
IATI describes development and humanitarian activities and is an interoperability profile rather than a universal Initiative master.
adversarial_checks: Reject an initiative without a resolvable identity, source profile, case for change, mandate or accountable sponsor.
Reject silent conversion of an Initiative into a Project, Program, Campaign or Operation and reject identity reuse across the formalization boundary.
Reject approval, delivery, outcome, benefit or causal impact inferred only from a label, budget line, activity completion or linked project state.
Reject silent option, scope, membership, roadmap, lifecycle, metric or decision mutation and any history rewrite.
Reject an agent operation that selects an option, admits work, commits funding, formalizes delivery, exposes protected data or destroys held evidence without delegated authority.

boundaryDecision.rationale: Two axes must not be conflated. On the record plane the registry classifies how Vercy files the record (the standalone-mm family of values); that is a filing classification and never a valid subject-model entry kind. In this pack frozen_context arrived empty, so the record-plane value could not be re-read and is carried as a publication hold. On the subject-model axis the defensible schema enum is aggregate: one Initiative root owns a bounded cluster of initiative-scoped assertion classes (mandate, case for change, options, memberships, dependencies, roadmap and gates, assignments and envelopes, lifecycle and formalization events, metric definitions, evaluations, access and retention state) under a single consistency and authority boundary, while every party, strategy, objective, policy, project, program, portfolio, campaign, activity, experiment, capability, product, service, resource, budget, contract, risk, issue, decision, metric, observation, dataset and audit master stays external and is referenced by identity. entity would understate the owned child-assertion classes and the append-only released-history invariant; relationship would misread the membership assertions as the subject rather than as owned children; pattern or mixin would deny the model its own identity and lifecycle; registry would misread a governed subject as an index of others. Aggregate is accepted as stated by the active provider.

decisions.concept: Aggregate root is Initiative, not a work-collection index
decisions.rationale: The consistency boundary is the initiative itself: it owns identity, lineage and initiative-scoped assertions, and every neighbour is referenced rather than contained. That is what makes a single root defensible instead of a thin index over external work.

decisions.concept: Formalization mints a new master identity with typed derivation and handover
decisions.rationale: This is the one rule preventing Initiative from collapsing into Project, Program, Campaign or Operation. It is asserted consistently in scope_statement, boundary_notes, patch_rules, policies, adversarial_checks, the formalize-derive finding and the formalize-or-transfer function. Cross-read for contradiction and none found.

decisions.concept: Ownership boundary excludes all neighbour master lifecycles
decisions.rationale: Twenty-four findings touch strategy, work, resources, budgets, risks, requirements and metrics, which invites drift into a universal work model. Each finding is written as a reference plus an initiative-scoped assertion, and the policies block states ownership does not transfer, so the breadth is contained.

decisions.concept: Composition by membership assertion without lifecycle cascade
decisions.disposition: accepted with a required explicit non-cascade rule
decisions.rationale: The linked-work finding says the initiative owns membership of externally owned work. The delete rule covers the initiative's own working copies but never states that cancelling, closing or disposing of an initiative must not cascade to member work objects. Add that sentence before canonical promotion.

decisions.concept: Templated question layer (25 of 72 provenance, 24 of 72 validation, near-identical q02 and q03)
decisions.disposition: rejected as canonical-grade, deferred for remediation
decisions.rationale: Every finding repeats the same two boilerplate questions with only the finding name substituted, so the interrogative layer carries little finding-specific content and cannot drive differentiated research. Tolerable in a reviewable draft, not acceptable for canonical promotion.

decisions.concept: SRC-001 and SRC-002 ISO catalogue abstracts cited as boundary support
decisions.rationale: Both are flagged primary_source false and are catalogue abstracts, yet they support the Project and Program boundary distinction and three functions. An abstract can evidence that a standard exists and what it is titled; it cannot support a semantic distinction. Extend the existing no-conformance omission to these specific support claims.

decisions.concept: ArchiMate version split between SRC-003 (3.1 exchange schema) and SRC-004 (3.2 certification program)
decisions.disposition: hold on crosswalk target version, SRC-004 rejected as a semantic source
decisions.rationale: A certification-program page is not a language specification, while the crosswalk finding promises pinned source and target versions. Either pin 3.1 to match the only specification-bearing source or add a 3.2 specification source before the interoperability claim is published.

decisions.concept: Retention, disposition and tombstone rules grounded in SRC-014 UK National Archives guidance
decisions.disposition: accepted as jurisdiction-scoped, rejected as a universal basis
decisions.rationale: The guidance is UK public-records specific. The model already delegates retention class and trigger to Dimension policy and lists jurisdiction dependence under regional assumptions, so the citation must stay scoped rather than be generalized into a cross-sector retention rule.

decisions.concept: Access default deny with field redaction modelled as artifact projection rather than a fifth scope
decisions.rationale: Keeping redaction as a projection over the four declared scopes (bundle, layer, finding, artifact) avoids a scope taxonomy that would drift from the structure, and the exception rule already demands cited authority, minimum necessary, time limits and separate logging.

decisions.concept: Artifact identity rule versus uniform artifact form across all twenty-four artifacts
decisions.rationale: The identity strategy (initiative id plus assertion or event id, never name, date, timestamp or digest alone) is correct and applied consistently. But a tamper-evident access log, a retention tombstone and a crosswalk record are not one artifact form, and an append-only log is poorly described as a serial assertion record. Differentiate before promotion.

decisions.concept: Registry Project parent link versus the Initiative-is-not-a-Project invariant
decisions.disposition: deferred to relationship-contract adjudication, published as a hold
decisions.rationale: The declared omissions state no approved relation rows exist and that the Project parent link remains a hold. A Project parent for an object that may precede or span projects would contradict the central invariant, so it must not ship as approved; as an unapproved hold it does not block a reviewable draft.

decisions.concept: Coverage checklist marking all sixteen dimensions covered
decisions.disposition: rejected, downgrade composition and interoperability to partial
decisions.rationale: The same package admits unapproved relation rows and an unpinned ArchiMate target version, which contradicts a blanket covered status for those two dimensions. The self-assessment must match the omissions block or the draft misrepresents its own maturity.

decisions.concept: Operation named as a formalization target but absent from the out-of-scope master list
decisions.disposition: accepted with a required editorial fix
decisions.rationale: The formalize-or-transfer function and the lifecycle finding both target an Operation master and the synonym exclusion names Operation, yet the out-of-scope master-lifecycle list omits it. Add Operation so the ownership boundary is symmetric across all named formalization targets.

decisions.concept: Source pins dated at or near the audit date (Green Book 2026, business-case guidance updated 30 June 2026, NIST PF 1.1 draft, ArchiMate 3.2 accessed 2026-09-06)
decisions.rationale: A no-tools audit cannot confirm these editions, update dates or access dates. They are plausible and internally consistent, but the version pins carry real weight in the crosswalk and appraisal findings, so they must be re-fetched before the draft leaves reviewable status.

decisions.concept: Single-provider merge posture
decisions.disposition: accepted with empty add_findings and add_functions
decisions.rationale: Codex is the sole active provider under the owner waiver, so there is no second stream to merge from and no synthetic contributions may be invented. The ten functions already trace register, mandate, appraise, map, link, plan, assign, transition, formalize and observe across all six bundles with source_refs, leaving no orphan finding ungoverned.

publicationHolds: Live source and version verification is unresolved. Every URL, edition, update and access date must be re-fetched and confirmed before the draft leaves reviewable status, in particular The Green Book 2026, the business-case guidance updated 30 June 2026, NIST Privacy Framework 1.0 with the 1.1 initial public draft, the ArchiMate 3.2 certification page accessed 2026-09-06, and the IATI 2.03 activity and status codelist pages.

No independent second-provider review exists. The repository owner authorized waivers for Claude after repeated failures at 1800s, 900s, bounded 600s Sonnet and 300s Haiku, and for Grok. This local Codex adversarial audit is same-provider self-review and must never be presented as external validation; every publication artifact must carry a visible absence-of-external-review notice.

Relation rows remain held. No approved rows were supplied, and the proposed registry Project parent link stands against the model's own Initiative-is-not-a-Project invariant, so the relation set must publish as explicitly empty and held pending relationship-contract adjudication.
No ISO 21500 or ISO 21502 conformance or clause-level claim may appear anywhere in the published artifact, since only catalogue abstracts were read and those citations are existence references only.

The coverage checklist must be corrected from all-covered to partial for composition and interoperability before publication so the self-assessment matches the declared omissions rather than overstating maturity.

The frozen registry record could not be re-read because frozen_context arrived empty in this audit pack. The record-plane classification and registry_id vr.wm-act-030 must be re-confirmed against the frozen record before publication, independently of the accepted aggregate subject-model kind.
Independent external review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this codex-only result remains a reviewable draft.

model.name: Program / Portfolio
model.purpose: Represent a governed program or portfolio that coordinates or selects components to advance strategy and realize outcomes or value while preserving the identity and lifecycle of every component master.
model.scope_statement: Owns the program-or-portfolio root and lineage, required profile discriminator, mandate and governance, strategy alignment, aggregate scope, component membership and dependencies, outcome and benefit logic, roadmaps or horizons, aggregate assignments and allocation decisions, prioritization or sequencing, lifecycle, metrics and aggregate evaluation, projections, access and retention. Party, strategy, objective, project, program-as-component, product, operation, benefit, resource, budget, contract, risk, issue, decision, observation, dataset, policy and generic audit masters remain external.
in_scope: Program or portfolio identity, profile, mandate, governance, strategy alignment, scope, component membership, dependencies and decision rights
Objectives, outputs, capabilities, outcomes, benefits, disbenefits, impacts, roadmaps, tranches or horizons, transition, resources, funding references, prioritization, balancing and controls
Authorization, component changes, start, pause, rebalance, termination, closure, metrics, observations, evaluation, learning, interoperability, access, retention and agent operations
out_of_scope: Party, strategy, objective, project, product, operation, benefit, resource, budget, contract, risk, issue, decision, observation, dataset, policy or audit-log master lifecycle
Treating Program and Portfolio as synonyms, admitting an instance without a profile, or inferring outcome, benefit or causal impact from completion, spending or output alone

Implementing scheduling, portfolio optimization, financial accounting, procurement, workforce management, risk engines, analytics platforms or universal legal compliance and claiming full ISO conformance from public abstracts

boundary_notes.distinction: A program coordinates related components to deliver outcomes and realize benefits; a portfolio selects, prioritizes and balances investments aligned to strategy, and components need not be related. The root is shared only under a required profile and profile-specific rules.
The aggregate owns membership and coordination or selection assertions, while each external component keeps its own purpose, owner, lifecycle, plan, resources and evidence.
The aggregate records versioned alignment and contribution claims; authoritative strategy, objective and policy masters remain external.
The aggregate owns its results logic and realization plan, while observed results and benefit masters remain source-qualified and completion does not establish causation.
The aggregate owns scoped assignments, rankings, allocations, control and evaluation views; source systems retain authoritative transactions, capacities, risks, decisions and observations.

boundaryDecision.rationale: Two axes must stay separate. On the record plane the frozen registry classifies this as a standalone model record (standalone-mm); that is a storage and publication classification of the Vercy record and is not a member of the subject-model enum, so it must never be emitted as entry_kind. On the subject plane the modelled thing is an invariant-enforcing root: it owns profile, mandate, governance, membership, allocation, sequencing, lifecycle and evaluation assertions, while every component, party, strategy, benefit, budget, risk, decision and observation master is referenced only by external identity and retains its own lifecycle, owner and evidence. That is an aggregate. It is not an entity, which would not carry the membership and allocation invariants; not a registry, which would hold the catalogue of investments but neither the mandate, reserved decision rights nor the root lifecycle; not a relationship, since membership is one owned assertion class inside the root rather than the root itself; and not a pattern, mixin, classifier or event. Accepted for a reviewable draft. The Programme-versus-Portfolio split remains a deferred contingency guarded by the required profile discriminator and profile-specific rules, not a present reclassification.

decisions.concept: Aggregate root: one profiled programme-or-portfolio root
decisions.rationale: The root owns membership, allocation, sequencing and lifecycle assertions while every component and master is referenced by external identity, which is the defining invariant boundary of an aggregate rather than a plain entity.

decisions.concept: Alternative entry kind: portfolio-as-registry
decisions.rationale: A registry would own only the catalogue of investments; this root also carries mandate, governance, reserved decision rights, benefit logic and its own lifecycle, so registry understates the invariants it enforces.

decisions.concept: Record-plane value standalone-mm versus subject-model entry kind
decisions.disposition: reclassified to the schema kind aggregate
decisions.rationale: standalone-mm describes how the registry stores and publishes the record, not what the modelled subject is; the two axes must be published separately so the enum value remains a subject-model claim.

decisions.concept: Split into separate Programme and Portfolio models
decisions.rationale: The required profile discriminator plus profile-specific selection-versus-sequencing rules suffices for a reviewable draft; a split needs implementation evidence of unsafe ambiguity that this pack does not yet contain.

decisions.concept: ISO SRC-001 to SRC-005 marked primary_source true
decisions.disposition: rejected as stated; downgrade to abstract-level support
decisions.rationale: The pinned URLs are catalogue pages and the pack's own omissions admit full text was unavailable, so tier-1 authority is fair but primary-source retrieval is not established and must not underwrite clause-level claims.

decisions.concept: Source refs on the retention and the access findings
decisions.disposition: rejected as source support; relabel as Vercy house policy
decisions.rationale: SRC-004, SRC-006, SRC-010 and SRC-012 cover governance, provenance and timestamps; none is a records-retention or privacy authority, so retention class, legal hold, tombstone and minimum-necessary disclosure rules are currently unsourced.

decisions.concept: Templated q02 provenance and q03 validation questions, 48 of 72
decisions.disposition: accepted for the draft, rewrite deferred
decisions.rationale: Identical wording across every finding gives no discriminating research prompt, but the questions are not wrong and deleting them would strip provenance and validation coverage before finding-specific replacements exist.

decisions.concept: Uniform six-bundle, two-layer, two-finding lattice
decisions.disposition: accepted with a deferred depth rebalance
decisions.rationale: Perfect symmetry indicates generated rather than domain-driven decomposition; component membership and dependency carries far more real variability than profile definition and identity does.

decisions.concept: Programme-or-portfolio profile embedded in the artifact identity strategy
decisions.disposition: accepted, conditional on an explicit supersession rule
decisions.rationale: Putting the profile in the identity tuple means reclassification cannot be an update, yet canon_and_patch defines only profile-safe successors and leaves profile-unsafe change entirely undefined.

decisions.rationale: Identity strategies, policies and boundary notes use programme-or-portfolio while the name and naming rule use the US spelling, which breaks deterministic artifact naming and crosswalk round-tripping.

decisions.concept: Access scopes bundle, layer, finding, artifact versus field-level minimum necessary
decisions.rationale: The default access rule and the audit requirements both assume field-level disclosure control and affected-field logging that the declared scope list cannot express, so one of the two must give.

decisions.concept: Benefit and change owner role responsibilities
decisions.rationale: Owning outcome definitions, baselines, targets and realization evidence reads as ownership of the external benefit master that out_of_scope explicitly excludes; the qualifier keeps the ownership boundary intact.

decisions.concept: Campaign and product neighbor distinctions in the profile boundary finding
decisions.rationale: The finding asserts distinctions from campaign and product masters, but its source refs cover only ISO project, programme and portfolio material, leaving those two boundary claims unsupported inside this pack.

decisions.concept: Coverage checklist marking all sixteen dimensions covered
decisions.disposition: rejected as stated; qualify interoperability, composition and capabilities
decisions.rationale: The same package admits abstract-only ISO support, unapproved relation rows and no dedicated stakeholder-engagement finding, so a uniform covered status overstates what has actually been verified.

decisions.concept: serial set true on all twenty-four artifacts
decisions.disposition: accepted for the draft, per-artifact adjudication deferred
decisions.rationale: The crosswalk and metric-definition records behave like versioned releases rather than serially numbered event artifacts, but a uniform default is safe while the naming token is being normalized.

Replace the forty-eight boilerplate provenance and validation questions with finding-specific probes, since their identical wording gives no discriminating research signal across twenty-four findings.
Assess RFC 9557 additional-information suffixes against the RFC 3339 timestamp rule and the separation of planned, decision, event, effective, observation, ingestion and knowledge times.
Collect implementation evidence on whether one profiled root or two separate Programme and Portfolio models is safer, and record the trigger that would force the split.
Reconcile the campaign, product and operation neighbor boundaries with the sibling subject models that own those masters, and attach source refs to each asserted distinction.
Attempt one bounded supplemental Grok review pass under the record-and-continue policy so the reviewable-draft hold can eventually be lifted by a genuinely independent provider.
