The subject is the observation act; identity is anchored on the immutable measurand triple of property, procedure and ultimate feature of interest, and the result's own patch rules treat any change to that triple as a new observation rather than a version.

decisions.concept: Splitting into a separate Observation Act (event) and Measurement Record (entity) model
decisions.rationale: OMS, SOSA, SensorThings and FHIR all address the act and its record as one thing. A split would create a mandatory one-to-one pair, duplicate identity resolution across both halves, and break the existing rule that a measurand change yields a new record rather than a new version of a shared act.

decisions.concept: Aggregate root scoped to the single observation record, with series, datastream and collection excluded
decisions.rationale: Membership is carried as outbound references plus effective inherited values, and the container keeps its own identity, extent and completeness accounting. The SensorThings datastream-level unit and observation-type binding is handled as a recorded mapping-loss case rather than absorbed, which keeps the boundary honest.

decisions.concept: original-acquisition-record claimed as an artifact of one observation record
decisions.disposition: flagged defect, accepted only with a stated cardinality
decisions.rationale: The identity strategy names run, batch and injection sequence keys, which routinely span many observations, so the artifact is many-to-one against the record that claims it. The draft must state the sharing cardinality and that immutability enforcement belongs to the electronic-records model, which the same result places out of scope.

decisions.concept: encoded-observation-representation identity strategy
decisions.disposition: flagged defect, correction required before candidate exit
decisions.rationale: Parent observation identifier plus encoding and profile identifier plus projected record version does not distinguish two projections of the same version made at different instants by different agents. The projection function already records agent and loss, so agent and instant, or the content digest, must be part of identity rather than adjacent metadata.

decisions.concept: result-payload-object identified locator-first
decisions.rationale: The artifact identity strategy leads with the payload locator issued by the storing system, while the model's own identity priority states that a file name, run sequence or similar value is never an identifier. Digest plus parent observation identifier plus zero-based part index should lead, with the locator retained as a resolution aid only.

decisions.concept: Uncertainty, traceability and conformity layer has no function
decisions.rationale: Three findings and twelve questions covering the model's distinctive metrology value are unreachable through the nine declared functions, and hold, embargo and derivation binding are similarly thin. No function may be added in single-provider mode, so this is carried as deferred research and a visible draft note rather than repaired here.

decisions.concept: access.scopes of bundle, layer, finding and artifact against an element-level default grant
decisions.rationale: The declared scopes are context-structure planes of the model document, while the default rule grants over instance elements such as identity, classification, status, result value, payload, subject references and the acquisition record. Without a stated mapping the deny-by-default rule is not enforceable by the access-policy model it delegates to.

decisions.concept: Unconditional release of decision rule and uncertainty alongside a published conformity statement
decisions.rationale: The exception is grounded in ILAC guidance, which the same result's regional assumptions limit to laboratories under an ILAC-arrangement accreditation body. Stated unconditionally in access.exceptions it over-claims, so it must be conditioned on the adopting Dimension's declared accreditation or regulatory regime.

decisions.concept: Cardinality grounded in the draft 2021 OGC working feature catalogue rather than published OMS/ISO 19156:2023
decisions.rationale: The anchor source of the entire boundary argument was not read: the OGC HTML exceeded the fetch limit and the ISO catalogue returned 403. The result discloses this and states required elements on its own authority, which is defensible for a draft but must not survive into candidate exit unverified.

decisions.concept: Composite source identifiers SRC-008 (seven JCGM documents) and SRC-012 (two ILAC guides)
decisions.rationale: One source id standing for several distinct publications makes every source_refs entry non-specific and makes the admitted absence of clause-level citation impossible to repair. Splitting into per-document ids is a prerequisite for any later conformance evidence.

decisions.concept: Registry placement under NAV.PHY.MAT.OBS with a WM-MAT identifier prefix
decisions.rationale: The evidence base spans geospatial, clinical, oceanographic and meteorological practice and the model is used as a cross-cutting substrate, which the materials nav path and MAT prefix understate. The registry record is frozen, so this is raised for the registrar rather than changed here.

decisions.concept: Empty frozen relationship contract against eleven asserted neighbour boundaries
decisions.rationale: The result names eleven owning neighbours and describes REFERENCE links to them, while parent_ids, contains_ids, aligned_model_ids and relations_ref are all empty and the contract is an empty array. The ownership boundary is therefore prose-only and unenforced, which the draft must state plainly.

decisions.concept: Tombstone treated as evidence of disposition while destruction is disclaimed
decisions.rationale: The audit requirement that disposition leave evidence of the policy and authority in force sits close to the disclaimer that this model never verifies or attests destruction. The draft must say the tombstone records a decision, not an erasure attestation, and that a persisted identifier may itself require assessment under the applicable data-protection regime.

decisions.concept: Absence and censoring expressed by coded reasons, never by null, blank or zero, and unit binding conditional rather than mandatory
decisions.rationale: Both survived challenge on their own evidence: nominal properties without magnitude and categorical or complex results make a mandatory unit unsupportable, while a censored or absent value silently encoded as zero is the specific failure this rule exists to prevent. The explicit dimensionless assertion closes the silent-omission path.

publicationHolds: Single-provider hold: Grok was waived by the repository owner on 2026-08-29 after repeated structured-output failures, so no independent second-provider review exists. The registry provenance line also credits a prior Claude adversarial audit, and this audit is likewise Claude, so every adversarial pass on this model is same-provider. The draft must carry this on its face and must not be read as cross-provider corroborated.

Live source and version verification hold: all sixteen source URLs, retrieval dates and version pins must be re-verified before publication, with specific attention to SRC-001 OMS 3.0 / OGC 20-082r4 / ISO 19156:2023, SRC-003 SOSA/SSN 2023 Edition, the SRC-008 JCGM set including the claimed JCGM 100:2008 Amd.1:2026, SRC-009 UCUM 2.2, SRC-010 QUDT 2.1 and the SRC-002 raw GitHub draft catalogue dated 2021-08-20.

Cardinality hold: the published normative OMS/ISO 19156:2023 requirements classes were never read. Every required-element and multiplicity claim rests on a draft working catalogue marked draft and dated 2021-08-20, and the result itself records a conflict between that catalogue's 0..* properties and the tighter cardinalities implied by SensorThings and FHIR. The model may not leave candidate status until each cardinality is re-verified against the published text.

Relationship-contract hold: the frozen contract is empty while the result asserts eleven owning neighbours and describes REFERENCE links to sibling models that are not registered. The draft must state that the ownership boundary is currently narrative and unenforced, and no downstream model may rely on those links until the contract is populated.

Artifact-identity hold: the encoded-observation-representation identity strategy cannot distinguish repeated projections of the same record version by different agents, the result-payload-object identity contradicts the model's own rule that a locator or file name is never an identifier, and the original-acquisition-record is many-to-one against the observations that claim it. These three defects must be corrected or explicitly disclosed in the published draft.

Entry-kind hold: the frozen registry carries entry_kind standalone-mm, which classifies the record plane only. Publication must state the subject-model kind as event alongside the record-plane value, so that no consumer treats standalone-mm as a semantic classification of the observation itself.
Independent second-provider review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this Claude-only result remains a reviewable draft.
deferredResearch: Obtain and read the published OGC 20-082r4 / ISO 19156:2023 requirements classes directly, then re-derive every required element and multiplicity in this model against them and retire the 2021 draft feature catalogue as the cardinality basis.

Split the composite source identifiers into one id per publication (JCGM 100, 101, 102, 106, 200, GUM-1, GUM-6; ILAC-G8 and ILAC-G17 separately), obtain parseable texts of GUM and VIM, and re-attach clause-level citations to the uncertainty, measurand and traceability findings.

Design an uncertainty, traceability and conformity function for the next revision so that the whole layer is reachable through the function set, together with functions for identifier resolution and duplicate reconciliation, provenance and derivation binding, and access classification, embargo and hold registration.

Verify WMO-No. 1192 WIGOS Metadata Standard and the QARTOD flag manual from their publications rather than a wiki page and a programme landing page, and re-assess the findings that currently lean on SRC-015 and SRC-016 as one of only three or four refs.

Refer the registry placement to the Dimension Registrar: NAV.PHY.MAT.OBS, the PHY.MAT.OBS domain tags, the WM-MAT identifier prefix and the 0.00 robotics factor all understate a model whose evidence spans geospatial, clinical, oceanographic and meteorological practice and whose SOSA grounding is sensor-centric.

Resolve whether measurement uncertainty is taken into account in the conformity decision (guard-band treatment under ILAC-G8) needs its own question, since the current interp-decision-rule and interp-risk-basis pair records the rule and the accepted risk but not how uncertainty entered the judgement.

Populate the relationship contract with the eleven asserted neighbours, assigning link types and stating which side owns each referent, so the ownership boundary becomes machine-checkable rather than prose.

bundles.name: Observation Act and Identity
bundles.description: Establishes what one observation record is: how it is identified and versioned, how it is classified, and how it binds to the procedure execution and the executing observer that produced it.
bundles.rationale: OMS and SOSA both define an Observation as the execution of an observing procedure, not as a value. Any agent operating on such records must first resolve identity, kind and the act itself before it can interpret anything else; SensorThings and FHIR both make identity and a typed classification mandatory entry points.

layers.name: Record Identity and Kind
layers.description: Identity, versioning and classification of the observation record and of the act it documents.

findings.name: Observation record identity and version identity
findings.description: How a single observation record is uniquely and stably identified, how the identity of the record is distinguished from the identity of the observation act, and how successive versions of the same record are identified without colliding with new observations.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Identity is pure reference data: a set of identifier values, their schemes and their version relations. It has no rendered or stored form of its own, and materialising it as a document would create a second, competing source of truth against the master system that issues the identifier.

findings.name: Observation kind and result-type classification
findings.description: How an observation is typed so that an agent can predict the shape of the result and the applicable interpretation rules: the observation type or result type, the domain category, and whether the observation is direct, derived, simulated or estimated.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Classification consists of coded values drawn from external vocabularies plus a profile reference. The code lists themselves are owned by vocabulary and profile registries, so this finding carries codes and references only and produces no artifact of its own.

layers.name: Act and Procedure Execution
layers.description: The binding between the observation record and the procedure, observer, host and deployment that executed it, together with the execution-specific parameters in force.

findings.name: Procedure, observer, host and deployment binding
findings.description: How the record names the observing procedure that was executed, the observer or system that executed it, the host or platform carrying that observer, and the deployment in force at the time, each by reference to the model that owns it.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Every element here is an outbound reference to a procedure, asset or deviation record owned by a sibling model. Reproducing those objects locally would duplicate their lifecycles; the record therefore stores only the reference, the version pinned at execution time and the deviation pointer.

findings.name: Observation parameters and influence quantities
findings.description: Named execution parameters and influence quantities that qualify the observation but are neither the measurand nor the result: settings, conditions applied, dilution or scaling factors, and any parameter needed to make the result reproducible.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Parameters are name-value-unit triples plus an inheritance statement. They are read and written as structured fields on the record, and the vocabularies that define parameter names belong to the property registry, so no separate artifact is warranted.

bundles.name: Subject and Property Binding
bundles.description: What was observed and on what: the feature of interest chain including any sample that stood in for it, and the observable property and measurand actually determined.
bundles.rationale: OMS requires an observation to name its feature of interest and exactly one observable property, and distinguishes the proximate feature (often a sample) from the ultimate feature the result is about. Misbinding either makes the result uninterpretable, so these are separated from the result itself.

layers.name: Feature of Interest Chain
layers.description: The proximate and ultimate features of interest and the sampling chain that connects them.

findings.name: Proximate and ultimate feature of interest
findings.description: How the record states the feature the result is actually about and, where observation was indirect, the intermediate feature that was directly observed, so that a result taken on a sample is never mistaken for a result taken on the whole.
findings.inline_only_rationale: This finding carries two typed references and a short justification statement. Feature entities, their geometry and their naming history are owned by the entity models being referenced, so materialising them here would duplicate another model's records.

findings.name: Sample linkage and sampling-chain reference
findings.description: How an observation made on a sample records which sample, where that sample sits in a sub-sampling or derivation chain, and which preparation steps had been applied before the observation, without absorbing the sample lifecycle.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The sample, its collection act, its preparation steps and its custody are owned by the sample model. This finding exists to pin the exact sample state that applied at observation time, expressed entirely as references and coded qualifiers, so it must not carry sample artifacts.

layers.name: Observable Property and Measurand
layers.description: The property observed and the fully qualified measurand, including the conditions that make the quantity intended to be measured unambiguous.

findings.name: Observable property binding
findings.description: How the record names exactly one observable property by reference to a governed vocabulary, distinguishes the property from its quantity kind, and handles properties that are only definable relative to a method.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The property term, its label, its dimension and its governance all live in the vocabulary registry. This finding contributes only the pinned reference, the derived quantity-kind link and two discriminating flags, which are structured fields rather than a document.

findings.name: Measurand specification and stated conditions
findings.description: The quantity intended to be measured, stated completely enough to be unambiguous: the property, the feature or matrix it is measured in, and the conditions (temperature, pressure, basis, fraction, time base) under which it is defined.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The measurand specification is a compact structured statement attached to the record. Where a fuller specification exists it belongs to the method document owned by the procedure model, so this finding deliberately holds the statement and its conditions inline rather than duplicating a method artifact.

bundles.name: Result, Quantity and Uncertainty
bundles.description: The result itself: its value and datatype, its unit and quantity binding, its absence or censoring, the uncertainty attached to it, the traceability that makes it comparable, and the interpretation or conformity statement drawn from it.
bundles.rationale: OMS, SensorThings and FHIR all model the result as a typed slot that can hold simple, complex or absent values, while VIM and GUM require a measurement result to consist of a measured value together with information about its uncertainty. Separating value, unit, absence, uncertainty, traceability and interpretation prevents the common failure of storing a bare number.

layers.name: Result Representation
layers.description: How the result value is represented, dimensioned and qualified when it is missing or bounded.

findings.name: Result value, datatype and cardinality
findings.description: How the result payload is carried for simple scalars, categorical values, vectors, components, coverages, images and time-series blocks, including how the declared datatype constrains the payload and how multi-component results relate to their parent.

findings.name: Unit of measure and quantity binding
findings.description: How the unit of a quantitative result is recorded unambiguously by naming both the code system and the code, how series-level unit defaults are reconciled with record-level values, and why conversion is forbidden without recording it.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Unit binding is a pair of coded references plus a conversion audit stub. The unit definitions, conversion multipliers and dimensional vectors are owned by the unit registry, and duplicating them locally would risk drift from the governed code system.

findings.name: Absent, censored and bounded results
findings.description: How the record expresses that no value exists, that a value is bounded rather than determined (below detection or quantitation limit, above range), or that a value was suppressed, so that absence is never encoded as zero or as an unexplained null.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Absence and censoring are expressed as coded reasons, bounds and references to limits established by the method model. There is nothing to render or store as a separate object, and creating one would encourage treating a censored value as though it were a determined value.

layers.name: Uncertainty, Traceability and Interpretation
layers.description: What makes the result usable as evidence: its stated uncertainty, its metrological traceability, and any interpretation or conformity statement drawn from it.

findings.name: Measurement uncertainty statement
findings.description: How the uncertainty associated with the reported value is stated so that it can be used: the kind of uncertainty, its value and unit, the coverage factor and coverage probability where expanded, and the basis on which it was evaluated.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The uncertainty attached to a single result is a small set of numeric fields plus a reference. The uncertainty budget itself is a method-level document owned by the procedure model; holding a copy here would create a second budget that could diverge from the validated one.

findings.name: Metrological traceability declaration
findings.description: How the record declares that the result is related to a stated reference through a documented unbroken chain of calibrations, by reference to the calibration and reference-material evidence in force at the time of observation.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Calibration certificates and reference-material certificates are governed artifacts of the calibration and reference-material models, with their own issuance, validity and revocation lifecycles. This finding records only which of them were in force and whether the chain is complete, so it must not carry copies of them.

findings.name: Reference ranges, interpretation and conformity statements
findings.description: How a result is turned into a judgement: the reference range or specification limit it was compared against, the resulting interpretation code, and, where a statement of conformity is issued, the decision rule identifier and the risk basis behind it.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The judgement recorded here is a set of coded values and references. The decision rule is defined and approved elsewhere, and the test report or certificate that publishes the conformity statement is a deliverable of the reporting model, so no artifact is created at the level of a single observation record.

bundles.name: Time, Place and Context
bundles.description: The temporal frame that makes a value locatable in time, the resampling semantics that make it safe to aggregate, and the spatial and environmental context in which it was obtained.
bundles.rationale: OMS, SOSA and SensorThings all separate phenomenon time from result time and admit a distinct valid time, and the OGC Timeseries Profile shows that a value cannot be correctly resampled without interpolation and aggregation semantics. SSN adds operating conditions as a context of validity. These are distinct decision surfaces and are grouped apart from the result.

layers.name: Temporal Frame
layers.description: The several distinct times attached to an observation and the semantics governing how the value behaves across time.

findings.name: Phenomenon, result, valid and ingestion time
findings.description: How the record distinguishes the time the observed phenomenon applies to, the time the result became available, the interval over which the result is asserted to be valid, and the time the record was captured or ingested, each with an explicit offset.
findings.inline_only_rationale: All temporal context is a small set of timestamp fields plus a clock-context object. It is queried and compared as data, never rendered or exchanged as a standalone object, and materialising it would break the atomicity of the record.

findings.name: Aggregation, interpolation and sampling regime
findings.description: The semantics that determine how a value may be resampled, aggregated or compared: whether it is instantaneous, averaged, accumulated or cumulative, over what duration, and how interim values between observations may be inferred.
findings.inline_only_rationale: These are interpretation flags and durations carried on the record so that a single observation remains safely resamplable in isolation. The series that supplies the defaults is a separate aggregate with its own identity, so this finding holds effective values only and produces nothing storable.

layers.name: Spatial and Environmental Context
layers.description: Where the observation applies and under what conditions the observing system was operating.

findings.name: Observation location, geometry and spatial reference
findings.description: How the record states the position or extent the result applies to, distinguishing the location of the observer from the location of the feature or sample, and always naming the coordinate reference system and vertical datum.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Geometry and its reference frame are structured values on the record. Station, site and sample geometry are owned by the corresponding entity models; this finding records what was effective for this observation and flags inheritance rather than storing a spatial document.

findings.name: Operating and environmental conditions of validity
findings.description: The conditions under which the observing system was operating and the environment surrounding it, which bound the applicability of any stated system capability such as accuracy, resolution or detection limit.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Capability statements, siting classifications and maintenance records belong to the observing-system and facility models. This finding contributes only the conditions effective at the act and the verdict against declared capability, which are fields on the record.

bundles.name: Quality, Validation and Lifecycle
bundles.description: How the record moves through its states, how it is corrected, what quality judgements have been recorded against it, and who is responsible for it.
bundles.rationale: FHIR makes observation status a mandatory modifier element, QARTOD shows quality flagging as a documented layer distinct from the value, MHRA requires original records and controlled amendment, and PROV-O supplies the responsibility model. Together these form the trust surface of an observation record and are separated from the measurement content.

layers.name: Record Lifecycle
layers.description: The states an observation record can occupy and the controlled transitions between them.

findings.name: Record status and permitted transitions
findings.description: The lifecycle states of an observation record from provisional capture through review to final, amended, superseded or retracted, and the rules governing which transitions are permitted, by whom and with what evidence.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Status and its transition history are coded fields on the record. The tamper-evident audit trail that independently attests to those transitions is owned by the electronic-records model, so this finding must record state without producing or claiming an audit artifact.

findings.name: Amendment, correction and supersession
findings.description: How a result that must change is handled: whether by amendment in place with a reason, by issuing a superseding record, or by retraction, always preserving the prior content and the reason for change.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Amendment is expressed by a mechanism code, a reason and version pointers. The preserved prior content lives as an earlier version of the same record rather than as a distinct artifact, and downstream notification is executed by the distribution model, not here.

layers.name: Quality Assessment
layers.description: Quality judgements recorded against the observation and the evidence supporting them, recorded but never evaluated here.

findings.name: Quality flags and quality-control outcomes
findings.description: How quality judgements produced by external quality-control procedures are attached to the record: the flag value, the code list it comes from, which test produced it, when, and by which agent, without this model owning the tests or their execution.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Flags are coded outcomes recorded on the record. Test definitions, thresholds, execution and re-evaluation belong to the quality-control model; carrying an evaluation artifact here would imply ownership of the evaluator, which this model explicitly does not have.

findings.name: Validation and verification evidence references
findings.description: How the record points to the evidence that supports its acceptance: control results, replicate or duplicate observations, blanks, spikes, proficiency-test outcomes and review sign-offs, each held by the model that owns it.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Every item here is a pointer to evidence owned elsewhere: control observations are themselves observation records, acceptance criteria belong to the method model, and signatures belong to the electronic-records system. Materialising an evidence pack here would copy other models' records and create a second, unmanaged source of truth.

layers.name: Provenance and Responsibility
layers.description: Where the record came from, what it was derived from, and who is accountable for it.

findings.name: Provenance chain and derivation
findings.description: How the record states what generated it, which prior entities it used or was derived from, and how the original acquisition record is preserved so that the reported value can be traced back to what the instrument or observer actually produced.

findings.name: Ownership, attribution and responsible agents
findings.description: Who owns the record, who is attributed as its producer, which organisation is the authoritative source for which part of it, and who may be contacted about it.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Ownership and attribution are reference fields pointing at organisation, agent and contact records maintained by directory models. Copying those records here would duplicate an external register that changes on its own schedule.

bundles.name: Governance, Access and Interoperability
bundles.description: How the record is protected and retired, how it is expressed for exchange without losing meaning, how its identifiers resolve across systems, and how it declares its membership in larger collections.
bundles.rationale: DCAT governs access rights, licence and versioning for published data; MHRA imposes retention and archiving duties; SensorThings, FHIR and OMS provide independent encodings that this model must be projectable into. These are governance and projection concerns, deliberately separated from measurement semantics so that storage and interface remain projections.

layers.name: Access and Retention
layers.description: Classification of the record for disclosure and its binding to a retention and disposition policy.

findings.name: Access classification and disclosure constraints
findings.description: How the record declares its sensitivity, the licence or access rights under which it may be used, and any constraint arising from personal, commercial or security sensitivity of the observation or its subject.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Classification, licence and embargo are declared values on the record. The policies that define the classification scheme and the enforcement point that honours them belong to the access-policy model; this finding must not imply that it enforces anything.

findings.name: Retention, disposition and tombstoning
findings.description: How long the record and its payload must be kept, which policy determines that, what disposition decision was reached, and what evidence remains after the record is destroyed.
findings.inline_only_rationale: This finding records the policy binding, the decision and the tombstone as data. The retention policy itself is authored by the adopting Dimension's records policy and the physical destruction is executed by the storage platform, so neither may be represented as an artifact owned here.

layers.name: Interoperability and Membership
layers.description: Alignment to external observation standards, resolution of identifiers across systems, and membership in collections and series.

findings.name: Standard alignment and encoding binding
findings.description: Which external observation standards this record is aligned to, which elements map cleanly, where mappings are lossy, and how the record is projected into a named exchange encoding without the encoding becoming the semantics.

findings.name: Identifier resolution and cross-system correlation
findings.description: How identifiers on and around this record resolve to the things they name, how the same observation is correlated across systems that assign their own keys, and how duplicate or conflicting records are detected and reconciled.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Resolution bindings, correlation keys and reconciliation outcomes are reference data attached to the record. The resolvers, registries and matching services that operate on them are external systems whose behaviour this model describes but does not own.

findings.name: Collection, datastream and series membership
findings.description: How a single observation declares its membership in the collections, datastreams, series or composite observations that contain it, and which properties it inherits from them, without absorbing the containing aggregate's identity or completeness accounting.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Membership is expressed as outbound references plus the effective inherited values. The container aggregate has its own identity, extent, completeness accounting and publication lifecycle, so representing it as an artifact here would take ownership of another model's object.

EM-STR-02.content:
# EM-STR-02 local synthesis

## Disposition

- Profile WM-KNW-011 for Objective, Key Result and Target. These are role- and naming-regime variants of the same governed objective identity, not separate model roots.
- Reuse WM-XCT-025 only as the observation value/method/time/uncertainty mixin on a WM-MAT-008 observation host. The mixin owns no record identity.
- Add one identifier-unassigned **Outcome and Benefit Realization** aggregate containing independently addressable Outcome, Benefit/Disbenefit and Attribution Claim records under one benefits-register master.
- Profile reserved WM-ACT-034 Assessment / Evaluation for Value Assessment. Reference the unassigned Metric Definition candidate from EM-DAT-05 and work/deliverable records from EM-WRK-03.

Objective states a desired future condition and is never a metric. Key Result is an objective-role record with mandatory measure binding. Target binds comparison operator, baseline/target periods and values to an exact Metric Definition revision. A metric revision change requires an explicit methodological restatement; it cannot silently re-baseline the target.

Outcome is an asserted change in a subject's state, distinct from a deliverable and from the observations that evidence it. Benefit is a governed expected/forecast/partially-realised/realised/reversed claim over one or more outcomes. Disbenefit uses the same lifecycle with negative polarity. Planned effects remain forecasts until final or amended observations support the change for the declared phenomenon period.

Attribution Claim belongs to the Benefit aggregate and records contributor, share with uncertainty interval, method, evidence and adjudication. Shares are reconciled against one benefit identity and period. Portfolio/programme and constituent-project claims cannot both count the same contribution for the same period.

Value Assessment declares criteria, scale, method, evidence and conclusion. Incompatible value and harm scales remain separate labelled dimensions; scalar netting requires an explicit commensuration method and preserves uncertainty.

## Invariants

1. Objective is not a metric; targets pin exact metric-definition revisions.
2. Metric change never silently changes an existing target or baseline.
3. Deliverable completion does not prove an outcome.
4. Realisation needs qualified observations whose phenomenon time falls within the realisation window.
5. Expected and realised claims coexist; realised never overwrites expected history.
6. Missing measurement is an explicit absent reason, never zero.
7. Adjudicated attribution shares per benefit and period cannot exceed one.
8. Programme and constituent-project contribution claims cannot double count.
9. Disbenefit is polarity, not a separate model, and cannot be netted without method.
10. Units, scale versions, method, observation times and uncertainty travel with every value.

## Scenario result

Two projects claim 0.6 and 0.5 of one retention benefit, so both claims remain unadjudicated until reconciled to a non-overlapping total. Delayed measurement leaves the benefit forecast with `measurement-pending`; later evidence produces partial realisation with uncertainty and preserves the late result time separately from the phenomenon period. A rise in support contacts is recorded as a disbenefit attributed to one project and remains a separate dimension because no commensuration method exists.

## Holds

Both bases are non-canonical reviewable drafts. The Outcome and Benefit aggregate lacks registry allocation; the WM-MAT-008, WM-ACT-034 and EM-DAT-05 crosswalks are incomplete; relationship contracts, metric pins, attribution authority and fixtures are absent. No runtime or installability claim is made.

# EM-LND-05 local synthesis

## Disposition

- Create a **Project, Program and Portfolio Landscape profile** over WM-ACT-029 with component resolution through WM-ACT-005.
- Do not create a catalogue/runtime identifier.
- DeliveryLandscape is a read-only projection; DeliveryScope is already owned by the corresponding program/portfolio or project.

## Boundary

The view owns no project, program, portfolio, product, team, cost, benefit, resource or membership assertion. WM-ACT-029 owns program/portfolio membership, prioritization, dependencies, allocation decisions and benefit logic. WM-ACT-005 owns project identity, baseline, cost facts, resource commitments and project scope.

A tracker project, board or epic tree is only a tooling container unless it resolves to an authoritative project or program/portfolio identifier.

## Membership and allocation

One project may participate in multiple roots. Each membership requires a role: `financial-consolidating`, `coordination-only` or `reporting-only`. At most one financial-consolidating membership may apply to a project, fiscal period and cost dimension.

Project–Product and Project–Team edges are M:N references. Products and teams retain their own masters. Resource contention is recorded against the resource owner's capacity and can only be displayed by the landscape.

Cost is asserted once by the project for a pinned baseline, period, currency, price base and data date. Views apply declared allocation shares after deduplicating the source fact. Benefit claims distinguish additive exclusive attribution from non-additive contribution.

## Invariants

1. Every node resolves to an authoritative project or program/portfolio ID.
2. Views never store monetary or benefit facts.
3. Roll-up deduplicates source facts before summation.
4. Allocation shares total at most 1.0 per fact/period/dimension.
5. Orthogonal decompositions, such as product and team, are not summed together.
6. Contribution claims are non-additive.
7. Project–Product and Project–Team remain M:N.
8. Every view declares authoritative, as-of replay or scenario class with exact time and criteria pins.
9. Scenario results cannot feed authoritative actuals or benefit realization.

## Acceptance result

One project serving two products and four teams retains one project cost fact. A product view may allocate it 60/40; a team view may separately decompose it by effort, but those views cannot be added. Shared team capacity conflicts remain owned by the resource source. A portfolio containing a program and its project directly still counts the project fact once.

## Holds

Both bases remain `publishableCanonical: false`. WM-ACT-029 relation rows are unapproved, the membership-role discriminator lacks source grounding, and cross-root deduplication scope needs validation. Program/programme artifact naming is unresolved. This checkpoint is not an installable release.
